messages:
ana: Hey infra team — we're onboarding a new dedicated customer and need help with cloud account setup + quota increases + VPC connectivity. Target regions: us-west-2 (primary) and eu-west-1 for DR. Need GPUs (p4d and p4de), extra ENIs, EIPs, and a PrivateLink endpoint to our control-plane. Opening thread to coordinate what we need from AWS.
raj: Can you paste the exact instance types and counts you're planning? Also need the customer AWS account IDs and the CIDR ranges for their VPCs.
nana: Correction: that's ana :) Planning: p4d.24xlarge x4 in us-west-2 for initial fleet, possible scale to x12 in 6 weeks. Also reserve p4de.24xlarge x2 in eu-west-1 for failover. Customer account IDs: 123456789012 (customer-prod), 210987654321 (customer-dr). Proposed CIDRs (customer side): 10.200.0.0/16 (prod), 10.201.0.0/16 (dr). Our VPCs: 10.10.0.0/16 (us-west-2), 10.20.0.0/16 (eu-west-1).
micah: Cool. Immediate quota items to request: GPU instance quota for p4d/p4de (limit bump), EC2 On-Demand vCPU? Might not apply if using dedicated hosts but likely need ENIs and EIPs bumped. Also ask for PrivateLink interface endpoint quota (ENIs per AZ). AWS support sometimes layers limits: EC2, EFA, Elastic IPs, and security group rules.
raj: We also need to think about route propagation for the peering and overlapping CIDRs (they don't overlap — ok). For VPC peering: ensure non-overlapping, update route tables in each VPC to point to the peering connection. For PrivateLink: we'll set up an interface endpoint in customer account to our service NLB in our account; that needs permission + cross-account endpoint-service.
nana: Added details for support case: requested quota increase numbers: us-west-2: p4d.24xlarge +12 (total request 16), ENIs +200, Elastic IPs +20; eu-west-1: p4de.24xlarge +4, ENIs +80, Elastic IPs +10. Also request increase for VPC Peering limit? (they usually allow many peering connections but we'll ask). Cost note: NAT Gateway charges will apply if we use them — customer prefers minimal egress cost.
micah: For NAT: suggest using centralized egress via a shared NAT in our transit VPC to reduce per-AZ NAT charges. Alternatively, use NAT instances for now to save cost — but less durable. Also note that EIP quota matters because NAT gateways need EIPs.
devops-ryan: FYI: created a support case with AWS: CS-2026-987654. They asked for the following in the case: account IDs, requested instance counts, AZ distribution, ENI count rationale, and ownership contact email. I attached the traffic profile doc and expected sustained throughput.
nana: Thanks Ryan — can you paste the case link/summary? I need the case ID for the customer comms.
devops-ryan: Case ID above. AWS replied requesting proof of business need and an architecture sketch. I uploaded the diagram and a short note: "Redwood Dedicated — cross-account PrivateLink + VPC peering for model inference fleet hosting customer-owned workload. Need GPU capacity for low-latency inference SLA." They put it into expedited review (we chose business-critical).
raj: Ok next: networking actions. Steps for peering + PrivateLink (high level):
1) Create VPC peering connection from our VPC (10.10.0.0/16) to customer VPC (10.200.0.0/16) in us-west-2 (CLI snippet below).
2) Add route table entries in our private subnets: 
```
aws ec2 create-vpc-peering-connection --vpc-id vpc-0abc1234 --peer-vpc-id vpc-0def5678 --peer-owner-id 123456789012 --region us-west-2
aws ec2 accept-vpc-peering-connection --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0aa11bb22
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-0aaa111 --destination-cidr-block 10.200.0.0/16 --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0aa11bb22
```
3) For PrivateLink: create NLB in our account, register targets (control plane ENIs), create endpoint service, allow principals (customer account ID), then customer creates interface endpoint in their subnets.
```
# create endpoint service
aws ec2 create-natgateway ... (NLB creation steps omitted)
aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint-service-configuration --network-load-balancer-arns arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:111:loadbalancer/net/my-nlb/...
# then set acceptance-required false or true depending
```
raj: We'll share a small terraform module for this so customer can self-service the endpoint creation.
nana: Who will own the security review for exposing PrivateLink to customer accounts? We need to ensure KMS/ECR access and restrict to only the interface endpoint.
micah: Security side: we need an IAM role and service principals locked to the customer account. Also ensure the NLB is internal and TLS is enforced between our control-plane and the customer endpoint. We'll run a short threat model — I can own that.
devops-ryan: Outcome & next steps: 
- Ryan: keep pushing CS-2026-987654 with AWS for GPU quotas (assigned).
- Micah: security review for PrivateLink and NLB TLS (ETA 2 days).
- Raj: terraform module for peering + endpoint (ETA EOD tomorrow).
- Ana: confirm final counts with customer and share contact email (you already have case ID).
nana: ack. I'll confirm counts and share billing contact. Also, quick ask: can someone estimate incremental monthly cost for NAT vs central transit NAT for the initial setup (4 p4d instances)? Might be large.
micah: Quick back-of-envelope: NAT gateway charge ~ $0.045/hr + $0.045/GB? (varies by region). For 4 large GPUs streaming model outputs it's not trivial. I'll run numbers and post in a follow-up.
cloud-support-bot: AWS Support Update (CS-2026-987654): "We have received additional information. Quota request is under review. Please expect response within 48-72 hours. If urgent, reply to the case with justification and attach architecture diagram."
nana: Great, thanks. I'll wait for AWS then start the terraform work with raj's module. If anyone sees obvious missing items (EFS? FSx? EBS throughput?), call it out here.
raj: Add EBS optimized IOPS and gp3 throughput targets to the request if you need sustained model cache performance — talk to perf team before finalizing numbers.
nana: Noted. Perf will chime in. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
